title: Randomly Shifted Steinhaus Longimeters and Buffon Discrepancy
summary: Let $Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a bounded convex domain. Steinerberger (2026) introduced the Buffon discrepancy problem: given length $L$, construct a one-dimensional set $S\subsetΩ$ such that the number of intersections of $S$ with a line $\ell$ approximates the Crofton-normalized chord length $$ \frac{2L}{π|Ω|}\cdot\mathcal{H}^1(\ell\capΩ).$$ Steinerberger proved a universal upper bound of order $L^{1/3}$ using a Steinhaus longimeter construction, and showed that the disk admits bounded discrepancy.
